subject: VALUE clause
notes: ONE SENTENCE, TWO INDEPENDENT CONJUNCTS, BOTH IMPLEMENTED WITH THE RIGHT SCOPES -- the two-arm shape this repo gets wrong most often, checked deliberately here. CONJUNCT 1 is NOT scoped to alphanumeric groups ("subordinate items within that group", full stop) and the code leaves it unscoped: MEASURED, `01 G VALUE "ABCD". 05 A PIC X(2) JUSTIFIED RIGHT.` and the SYNCHRONIZED twin both draw COBOL1702 (probes sr14_just, sr14_sync), and so does a JUSTIFIED subordinate of a GROUP-USAGE NATIONAL group (sr14_natgroup_just) -- the case a wrongly shared scope would have missed. CONJUNCT 2 IS scoped to alphanumeric group items per 13.18.29.4 GR3 ("that group item is an alphanumeric group item" -- cite.py --check OK) and the code states all three GR3 conjuncts: MEASURED, a COMP leaf draws COBOL1702 (sr14_comp), a COMP leaf TWO levels down draws it (sr14_deep_comp -- "subordinate to", not "immediately subordinate to"), an INHERITED group-level USAGE COMP draws it on the leaf (b_sr14_implicit_usage -- the "implicitly described" half), and the OVER-REJECTION CONTROL passes: a conforming national group `01 G GROUP-USAGE NATIONAL VALUE N"ABCD". 05 A PIC N(2). 05 B PIC N(2).` compiles and DISPLAYs [ABCD] (sr14_natgroup_ok), because a national group's subordinates take usage NATIONAL by 13.18.29.3's own rules and SR14's usage arm does not reach them. SR16 carries SR14 to the Format-2 carrier (IsGroupValueSubject reads TableValues). Edition-invariant: both negatives are pinned reject-at 85 2002 2014 2023, and Annex E records no change. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.GroupValue.cs:133-141 (conjunct 1 -- `sub.Justified || sub.Synchronized`, UNSCOPED) and :153-167 (conjunct 2 -- `if (!alphanumericGroup) continue;` then `SubordinateUsageOf(sub) is not { } usage || usage is Usage.Display`), both -> DiagnosticCatalog.GroupValueSubordinate (COBOL1702); the scope predicate is #IsAlphanumericGroup (:203-206, all three 13.18.29.4 GR3 conjuncts); the diagnostic's usage word comes from #UsageWord (:229-240), drift-tested by tests/WiseOwl.Cobol.Tests.Unit/UsageWordDriftTests.cs; the pass runs AFTER UsageInheritancePass so "implicitly" is honoured (BindPipeline.cs:43)
